title: Auto Layout Fundamentals
description: Learn how to build flexible, responsive card components using CSS layout techniques. Start with a fixed-size box and progressively enhance it with padding, flexbox, and media queries.

steps.title: Create a fixed-size box
steps.instruction: Every layout starts somewhere. Let's begin with the simplest possible component: a box with a hardcoded width and height. This is how many beginners approach layout, and it works—until you need it to adapt to different content or screen sizes.
steps.code: .card { width: 300px; height: 200px; background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e2e5eb; border-radius: 12px; }

steps.title: Add padding and content
steps.instruction: A box without content is just decoration. Let's add some inner text and padding to give our card breathing room. Padding creates space between the content and the edges of the container—one of the most fundamental layout concepts.
steps.code: .card { width: 300px; padding: 24px; background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e2e5eb; border-radius: 12px; } .card-title { font-weight: 600; font-size: 18px; color: #121726; } .card-body { font-size: 14px; color: #5a6375; }

steps.title: Use flexbox for layout
steps.instruction: Here is where things get powerful. Flexbox lets you control how children are arranged inside a container. By setting display: flex and flex-direction: column, child elements stack vertically with consistent spacing via the gap property—just like auto layout in Figma.
steps.code: .card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; width: 300px; padding: 24px; background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e2e5eb; border-radius: 12px; } .card-actions { display: flex; gap: 8px; margin-top: auto; }

steps.title: Make it responsive
steps.instruction: Fixed widths break on small screens. Replace the hardcoded width with max-width and use percentage-based sizing. Now the card gracefully adapts to its container—it never overflows, but it also never stretches beyond a comfortable reading width.
steps.code: .card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; width: 100%; max-width: 400px; padding: 24px; background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e2e5eb; border-radius: 12px; box-sizing: border-box; }

steps.title: Complete responsive card
steps.instruction: Let's bring it all together. A complete responsive card that adjusts padding and font sizes at different breakpoints using media queries. This is the CSS equivalent of responsive constraints in Figma—your layout adapts gracefully from mobile to desktop.
steps.code: .card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; width: 100%; max-width: 400px; padding: 16px; background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e2e5eb; border-radius: 12px; box-sizing: border-box; } @media (min-width: 640px) { .card { padding: 24px; gap: 16px; } .card-title { font-size: 20px; } }
